title: Board gender diversity and emissions performance: Insights from panel regressions, machine learning, and explainable AI
abstract: arXiv:2510.00244v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: With European Union initiatives mandating gender quotas on corporate boards, a key question arises: Is greater board gender diversity (BGD) associated with better emissions performance (EP)? To answer this question, we examine the influence of BGD on EP across a sample of European firms from 2016 to 2022. Using panel regressions, advanced machine learning algorithms, and explainable AI, we reveal a non-linear relationship. Specifically, EP improves with BGD up to an optimal level of approximately 35 %, beyond which further increases in BGD yield no additional improvement in EP. A minimum BGD threshold of 22 % is necessary for meaningful improvements in EP. To assess the legitimacy of EP outcomes, this study examines whether ESG controversies weaken the BGD-EP relationship. translated_title: 董事会性别多元化与排放绩效：来自面板回归、机器学习和可解释人工智能的见解
translated_abstract: arXiv:2510.00244v3 公告类型：replace-cross 摘要：随着欧盟倡议强制要求公司董事会实行性别配额，一个关键问题随之而来：更高的董事会性别多元化（BGD）是否与更好的排放绩效（EP）相关？为回答这一问题，我们基于2016年至2022年欧洲企业样本，考察了董事会性别多元化对排放绩效的影响。通过面板回归、先进的机器学习算法和可解释人工智能，我们揭示了一种非线性关系。具体而言，排放绩效随着董事会性别多元化的提高而改善，直至达到约35%的最优水平，超过该水平后，董事会性别多元化的进一步提升不再带来排放绩效的额外改善。至少22%的董事会性别多元化阈值是实现排放绩效有意义改善的必要条件。为评估排放绩效结果的真实性，本研究还考察了ESG争议是否会削弱董事会性别多元化与排放绩效之间的关系。结果显示无显著影响，这表明董事会性别多元化的作用源于治理机制而非象征性行为。此外，路径分……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究结合面板回归、机器学习与可解释人工智能发现，欧洲企业董事会性别多元化与排放绩效呈非线性关系，约35%为最优比例、22%为必要阈值，且ESG争议不削弱该关系，说明其作用源于治理机制而非象征性行为。
en_tdlr: Using panel regressions, machine learning, and explainable AI on European firms (2016–2022), this study reveals a non-linear relationship between board gender diversity and emissions performance—with an optimal level of ~35% and a minimum threshold of 22%—and shows ESG controversies do not weaken this link, indicating governance-driven rather than symbolic effects.
